sourceEvidence.observed: Almaden Library describes a photography exhibit where visitors can hear South Asian instruments using a QR code.
The library’s kickoff listing confirms the QR code lets visitors hear the instruments on display.
The Cantor Arts Center uses JANE! for the exhibition in both its title and description.
Stanford Libraries identifies Kim Bong-Jun with the Korean Minjung art movement and explains the name as people’s art.

events.title: Sounds of South Asia: an Exhibit

cases.refreshed: This interactive photography exhibit showcases several musical instruments from the South Asian subcontinent. Each exhibit will have a QR code that allows participants to listen to the sound of the instruments played in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. They include stringed, wind, and percussion instruments passed down through generations, which are still played around the Bay Area. Come and enjoy this exhibit, which starts on November 14, 2026, and closes on December 5, 2026. The exhibit is brought to you by the South Asians in Silicon Valley initiative at the SJSU King Library. Through this unique initiative, the SJSU King Library records, preserves, and shares the living legacy of the South Asian diaspora in the San Francisco Bay Area. Website: https://library.sjsu.edu/sasv
